title: Sentience context policy experiment
summary:
**Recommendation: keep stored Gemini summaries and persisted tool pruning; use the local governor for large tool loops. Leave native compaction off by default, especially on summarizer inputs.** These runs support that policy direction. They do not certify a global rollout to every agent.

The experiment completed **44 runs, 165 HTTP attempts, and 8 observed native compactions**. Of 36 chat-policy runs, 35 completed and passed all six fixture checks; one returned an Azure HTTP 500. The two OpenRouter route controls passed. Six additional runs compared summarizers. Each scenario has two fixture seeds, so these are controlled mechanism results, not population-level quality or p95 estimates.

**The compaction route is direct Azure:** `https://<azure-resource>/openai/v1/responses`, with `context_management=[{"type":"compaction","compact_threshold":160000}]` and `store:false`. Every observed compaction came from this route. OpenRouter handled Gemini summaries and the production-route control with compaction disabled. Raw response metadata confirmed GPT Sol and medium reasoning in both chat routes.

### The useful comparison: a 175k-token tool checkpoint, then three turns

| Policy | Input tokens / run | Normalized cost / run | Mean completion time | Checks passed | Native compactions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| Stored summary + pruning | 177,991 | $0.894 | 9.55s | 2/2 runs | 0 |
| Stored + governor | 91,038 | $0.460 | 8.92s | 2/2 runs | 0 |
| Stored + native | 178,503 | $0.730 | 12.45s | 2/2 runs | 2 |
| Stored + governor + native | 90,975 | $0.459 | 8.49s | 2/2 runs | 0 |

Adding the governor cut input **48.9%**, normalized cost **48.5%**, and observed mean time **6.6%** against stored summaries and pruning. Native compaction reduced normalized cost less and increased observed completion time **30.3%**. With the governor enabled, native never fired; the small difference between those two arms is ordinary run variation, not a native-compaction benefit. The fixture starts after source tools have returned: previous retrieval calls and their sunk costs are outside this comparison.

### Long conversation results

Stored summaries brought both conversation cases below the native boundary. Adding native produced **zero compactions** in every stored-summary conversation run. Replacing the existing stack with native alone at 175k reduced input about 30%, but **increased normalized cost 12.7%** and mean completion time about 12.8% versus raw replay. Cache reads and extra searches matter more than cumulative token totals alone.

Gemini reused its prompt cache between some summary arms. Therefore the raw ledger's lower summary charges for later arms do **not** establish that a governor or native flag made summarization cheaper. Compare their activation and request behavior, not those confounded cross-arm totals. The large-tool comparison above does not call the summarizer and avoids this confound.

### Summarizers need their own policy

| Summarizer on the same long transcript | Mean cost / run | Mean time | Audit code retained | Source IDs retained |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Production Gemini Flash | $0.322 | 17.88s | 2/2 | 0/2 |
| Sol without native compaction | $0.919 | 19.79s | 2/2 | 2/2 |
| Sol with native compaction | $0.730 | 18.92s | 1/2 | 1/2 |

In `summarizer-1-sol_native`, the expected audit code `ORCHID-7320` disappeared from the final summary. Plain Sol and Gemini retained it on the same fixture. Native compaction did not reduce total summarizer input: 359,663 tokens across two runs versus 357,165 for plain Sol. Both Gemini summaries omitted the fixture's reference labels `decision-17` and `invoice-22`; the chat runs recovered cited facts through tools. These artificial labels are not a complete test of production citation-ID handling. Keep recovery and test real citation formats before changing that contract.

### Policy to discuss

| Workload | Recommended policy | Evidence and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Long chat conversations | Keep Gemini summary at 60k estimated text and 20k tail; keep persisted pruning at 100k | Existing stack reduced context below native's boundary and preserved tested behavior |
| Large in-run search/tool results | Use the local governor: 140k estimated trigger → 120k target, protect newest 80k | Best measured incremental result; roll out to this workload with monitoring and a disable switch |
| Thread summarizer | Keep Gemini Flash on the source transcript; native off | Cheapest tested summarizer; native lost an exact fact and still processed the long input |
| Audio notes and other summarizers with search loops | Preserve the original transcript; consider the governor only for accumulated retrieval results | This is a transfer hypothesis from the tool fixture; audio-specific quality was not tested |
| One-shot extractors / core-memory synthesis | No blanket history compaction; keep source inputs intact within their existing budgets | Chat-history compression results do not establish extraction fidelity |
| Native Azure compaction | Keep experimental and opt-in until it beats the combined stack on relevant tasks | Useful versus some raw replay, but redundant after tested summary/governor layers and a summarizer fidelity failure remains |

The numeric thresholds use different units: the local policies use the existing character estimator; native uses provider-rendered tokens. The 175k conversation measured about 279k with the local estimator. This experiment does not establish that the threshold numbers are interchangeable or optimal.

### Accounting and scope

Dollar comparisons use **common Sol list rates**, including cache writes: $4/M ordinary input, $5/M cache writes, $0.40/M cache reads and $20/M output. Gemini cost includes OpenRouter's reported upstream BYOK charge and fee. These are **not verified Azure invoice savings**. See [Sol pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol) and [cache accounting](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching).

The batch measured 9,716,171 input tokens and 57,388 output tokens. Known usage corresponds to about $22.32 under the stated mixed normalization. One HTTP 500 has unknown usage and charge, so the total is incomplete. One separate preflight HTTP 400, from an invalid empty compaction configuration, is retained outside the 165-attempt batch; compaction-off requests were corrected to omit the field before measurement. No failed trial was rerun to turn the scoreboard green.

The harness uses the actual PersonalChatAgent factory, streamed Pydantic-AI event loop, production summary function, boundary/view logic, pruning/governor and persistence serializer. Tools and source data are synthetic. It does not exercise the full ChatService/UI, real users, repeated compactions in one conversation, route switching after compaction, or production traffic. Automatic chat transport retries were disabled consistently; the 500 remains visible. No new real-trace quality result is claimed.

Detailed runs follow. The separate summarizers.json contains the summarizer outputs.
